note: Public organization info only. Alumni connections are computed live in the app from your local donor list and are never stored in this file.

prospects.name: U-M MaizeRaise crowdfunding + Giving Blueday 2027
prospects.connection: B4P is a U-M student organization, and U-M runs crowdfunding pages for student orgs.
prospects.why: MaizeRaise fundraising pages can be requested any time. Giving Blueday 2027 is March 24, and student org registration is due Sunday, Dec 13, 2026, possibly earlier if it fills up. U-M's own Giving Tuesday application was due Oct 4, so that one has passed.

prospects.name: CSG Student Organization Funding Committee (SOFC)
prospects.connection: B4P is a recognized U-M student organization, so it's eligible.
prospects.why: Reliable funding for U-M orgs, but it reimburses expenses. It can't be donated to a cause, so it's best for covering shipping and event costs.

prospects.name: Planet Blue Student Innovation Fund
prospects.connection: U-M's Graham Sustainability Institute has already listed B4P activity. Recovering medical surplus cuts hospital waste.
prospects.why: Funds student projects that shrink U-M's environmental footprint. Recovering Michigan Medicine's surplus supplies fits directly. Grants go up to $30,000 for 2025/26.

prospects.name: U-M Center for Global Health Equity
prospects.ask: Student Org Global Health Equity Challenge
prospects.connection: U-M center focused on global health, which is exactly what B4P does by sending supplies to low-resource hospitals.
prospects.why: Runs a yearly pitch competition for student organizations that recently awarded more than $15,000 across five groups.

prospects.name: Michigan Medicine
prospects.connection: Existing partner: B4P collects Michigan Medicine's excess supplies. Several alumni are medical students there.
prospects.why: The partnership is already in place. Ask the Office of Development, or the environmental sustainability team (sustainability project manager Stephanie Peters), about supporting the program.

contact.name: Stephanie Peters
contact.title: Sustainability Project Manager (named publicly; email not listed)

sources.label: U-M story on B4P + Michigan Medicine

prospects.name: Henry Schein Cares Foundation
prospects.connection: No direct link yet. Very strong mission fit.
prospects.why: Its Global Product Donation Program and CARES Packages give medical supplies to nonprofits. Apply at least 6 weeks ahead. Recipients handle international shipping, which B4P already does.

prospects.name: Medline (Community Impact Grants)
prospects.connection: No direct link yet. Medical supply maker, strong mission fit.
prospects.why: Accepts Community Impact Grant and product donation requests on quarterly deadlines, the next one Dec 31. Lists a clear email contact.

prospects.name: Stryker
prospects.connection: Michigan company (Kalamazoo HQ). Medical device maker.
prospects.why: Reviews grant and charitable requests on a rolling basis through a web portal. Requests must be in at least 8 weeks ahead. Giving focuses on advancing healthcare.

prospects.name: Cardinal Health Foundation
prospects.connection: No direct link yet. Medical supply distributor.
prospects.why: Gave $6.3M across 232 grants in 2024, mostly to health systems and clinics. Grant programs are competitive and partly run through partner organizations.

prospects.name: Trinity Health Michigan (St. Joseph Mercy Ann Arbor)
prospects.connection: Ann Arbor hospital, local to B4P. Possible future source of surplus supplies.
prospects.why: Has an online sponsorship form, which needs 90 days' notice. The Ann Arbor hospitals also run an 'Investing in Our Communities' grant.

prospects.name: Henry Ford Health
prospects.connection: Michigan health system. Alumni work or train there.
prospects.why: Community Sponsorship Program funds 501(c)(3) public charities through an online form. Its priorities lean toward community health, so frame the request around health access.

prospects.name: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Foundation
prospects.why: Funds Michigan health initiatives and answers grant questions by email.

prospects.name: Michigan Health Endowment Fund
prospects.why: Large Michigan health funder. Applications go through RFPs, some needing a concept paper first, so this is a longer-term ask.

prospects.name: Ann Arbor Area Community Foundation
prospects.why: Funds 501(c)(3) groups serving Washtenaw County, so stress the local work, such as supplying Ann Arbor clinics. Contact details come from a third-party listing, so confirm them before emailing.

prospects.name: Rotary Club of Ann Arbor
prospects.connection: Local service club with an International Projects committee.
prospects.why: Its community grants focus on kids, but the International Projects committee fits B4P's global work. Asking to speak at a meeting is an easy first step.

prospects.name: Kiwanis Club of Ann Arbor Foundation
prospects.why: Funds Washtenaw County nonprofits, mostly for children and families, so it's a weaker fit. Watch for the next grant cycle.

prospects.name: DTE Energy Foundation
prospects.connection: Michigan company. Alumni have interned there.
prospects.why: Gives by invitation only, so cold applications don't get through. Best approached through an alum.

prospects.name: Ford Philanthropy
prospects.connection: Michigan company. Ford Community Corps works with Southeast Michigan college students.
prospects.why: Gives by invitation only. Ford Community Corps, which partners with Southeast Michigan schools, is the most realistic way in.

prospects.name: Google (matching gifts)
prospects.why: Matches employee donations 1:1 up to $10,000 with no minimum. An alum donates on Giving Tuesday and Google doubles it.

contact.title: Ask alumni here to submit a match
contact.method: Alum submits via employee giving portal

prospects.name: Bank of America (matching gifts)
prospects.why: Matches 1:1 up to $5,000 per employee per year.

contact.title: Ask alumni here to submit a match
contact.method: Alum submits via employee giving portal

prospects.name: Bloomberg (matching gifts)
prospects.ask: Employee match / Dollars for Your Hours
prospects.why: Matches 1:1 up to $5,000. Its Dollars for Your Hours program gives $2,500 for 25 volunteer hours. Employees submit through the Best of Bloomberg (BOB) function on the Terminal.

contact.title: Ask alumni here to submit a match
contact.method: Alum submits via BOB on the Terminal

prospects.name: JPMorgan Chase (matching gifts)
prospects.why: Matches 1:1 from $10 to $1,000, but only for gifts made through the company's own giving platform.

contact.title: Ask alumni here to give via the internal platform

prospects.why: The alum works in philanthropy at the firm, so they can best advise on firm giving or introduce you to the right people.
